# LESSONS-LEARNT.md - gotchas worth remembering

The running log of hard-won, non-obvious gotchas: the stuff that cost real debugging time and
would cost it again. Append here when a bug's root cause was surprising or system-wide. Keep each
entry a single bolded claim + the mechanism + the fix, at most ~4 lines. `PRINCIPLES.md` governs;
`CLAUDE.md` is the per-engine reference; this file is institutional memory - it does not restate a
rule already stated in either of those.

> First extracted from `CLAUDE.md` on 2026-07-13, re-merged 2026-08-23, trimmed 4 Sep 2026 (rules
> since folded into `PRINCIPLES.md`/`CLAUDE.md` retired; standing gotchas compressed).
> Per-feature decision logs live with their plan in `documentation/plans/<domain>/`.

**Housekeeping.** When a lesson's cause is fixed in code, or a regression test in
`sorento_crm_backend/tests/test_lessons_learnt_regressions.py` guards it structurally against
recurrence, retire the entry. When it merely duplicates a rule already stated in `CLAUDE.md` or
`PRINCIPLES.md`, retire it there too - one copy, one place. This log is append-mostly, not
append-only, or it stops being readable.

---

## Active

- **Respond.io `contact_id` ≠ `respond_io_id`.** Portal/complaint/stock-inquiry/purchase-request `contact_id` columns store the internal `respond_contacts.id` (UUID); the Respond inbox URL and message API need `respond_io_id`. Always resolve via `RespondContact` before building inbox URLs or calling Respond.io.
- **`respond_inbox_url` must be set at row creation** for the admin chat panel to work, and excluded from any `_editable_fields` payload application - a portal `_instantiate` missing it renders an empty chat with no error.
- **Vitest + jsdom does not implement `scrollIntoView`.** Guard with `ref.current?.scrollIntoView?.({...})` so component tests don't TypeError.
- **`DataGridTable` DOES mount rows under jsdom** - `useListingColumnPreferences` fetches column prefs and renders skeletons until it answers, and nothing answers under jsdom. Mock it (`vi.mock('@/lib/listing-column-preferences/useListingColumnPreferences', ...)`) and rows/badges/pagination assert normally.
- **A vitest wait that cannot fail is not a wait.** Two deploy-blocking CI failures (5-6 Sep 2026) came from specs waiting on something already true: `queryByText(/^loading/i)` once the spinner became `SectionSkeleton`, and `fireEvent.change` on a `<select>` before its lookup options existed (jsdom silently drops a value matching no option). A third: `const el = await screen.findBy...` followed by `fireEvent.click(el)` fires at a node React may have replaced across that await (a grid header swaps nodes when its rows land), and a click on a detached node is silent. All three pass on an idle machine and fail on a loaded runner. Use `waitForSectionLoaded` / `selectOption` / `tickCheckbox` from `sorento_crm_frontend/test-utils`: they re-query at the event and throw when they are guarding nothing.
- **Don't silently duplicate chat/list panels across domains.** Complaint, stock_inquiry, purchase_request all share the Respond chat panel via `components/common/RespondChatList.tsx` so ticks/dates/selection can't drift across the three.
- **AI assistant tool dropdown is sourced from the live MCP server, not the DB catalog.** Adding a tool to `sorento_crm_mcp.catalog.CATALOG` needs an MCP process restart to show up in `/api/v1/system/ai-assistant/tools`. `mcp_tools` (DB) is for AccessAgent ownership only.
- **A tool that doesn't proxy a CRM HTTP endpoint needs `external=True` on `ToolSpec`**, or `_compile_tool` 404s building an HTTP impl from `spec.method`/`spec.path`. Register the real impl separately (see `register_user_guide_tools`).
- **AI assistant chat renders raw text by default** - wrap in `ReactMarkdown` (`AIAssistantBubble.tsx`) or `**bold**`/links/lists show as literal characters. Internal links (`href` starts with `/`) route through `next/link`.
- **Guide-menu paths are annotated with markdown links to FE routes, not resolved at runtime.** Add new paths to `scripts/annotate_user_guides_routes.py` and re-run (idempotent).
- **User guides live in Outline at runtime, not the repo.** `documentation/user-guides/` is the editable copy; two-way sync via `scripts/sync_user_guides_outline.py push|pull` plus a 6h cron PR.
- **AI assistant must READ a guide before answering "how to"** - `user_guides_search` then `user_guides_read` then quote the steps with links intact, enforced by the **USER GUIDE PROTOCOL** system-prompt addendum, never just paste the doc URL.
- **Outline's web editor silently strips query-bearing markdown links on next save**, even though the API-pushed version stores them correctly - drops the moment a human opens+saves the doc in Outline UI. Verify via `documents.info` API immediately after any sync, never trust Outline's rendering; prefer `#fragment` deep-links over `?query` ones since fragments aren't in Outline's link-validator path.
- **`re.sub` replacement strings parse `\X` as backreferences.** Injecting a URL via `re.sub(pattern, f"...{url}...", text)` raises `re.PatternError` if `url` contains a literal `\u`/`\g`/`\1`-`\9`. Wrap in a lambda (`pattern.sub(lambda m, r=replacement: r, text)`).
- **Tailwind v4 `--primary` resolves to `oklch(...)`, not `H S% L%`** - `hsl(var(--primary) / 0.55)` is invalid CSS, silently dropped. Use `color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) X%, transparent)` for alpha overlays.
- **`GuideTargetSpotlight` needs a `MutationObserver` fallback for dialog-internal targets** - buttons inside `Dialog`/`Popover`/`DropdownMenu` only mount when the user opens the parent, so a fixed retry window expires first. Current strategy: rAF -> 5×200ms retry -> `MutationObserver` up to 30s (`app/components/common/GuideTargetSpotlight.tsx`).
- **Re-injecting a guide-authored deep link after LLM paraphrase needs a dynamic map, not the static `_ROUTE_MAP`.** The LLM often drops `[**Upload**](?guide_target=...)` to plain `**Upload**`; `_extract_guide_link_map(tool_calls)` scans tool outputs for every `[Label](URL)` pair and feeds it as `extra_map`, bold-only so a stray prose verb never gets auto-linked.
- **Two SLA systems share `conversation_sla_tracking`, discriminated only by `source_entity_type`.** Conversation SLA (n8n, one open per contact) has it NULL; form-SLA stage rows (per-entity, multi-active) have it set. Every contact-keyed query MUST filter with `conversation_tracking_scope()` (`sla_service.py`) or it falsely matches a form row - the original bug: an active form row 409'd n8n's conversation create.
- **Conversation-SLA create is idempotent, not 409.** Active row -> 200 with `already_active: true`, clocks/assignee untouched. Resolved row -> overwrite-in-place (event-log history survives, FK'd by tracking id). DB-level singleton via a partial unique index.
- **`create_event_log` interprets a NAIVE datetime as Malaysia time (UTC+8), but tracking columns store naive UTC.** Passing `tracking.due_at` straight in silently shifts it -8h. Wrap with `_to_aware_utc()` first.
- **Tests run on Postgres ONLY (PRINCIPLES.md governs the rule; this is the fixture-level detail).** `tests/_pg_fixture.py`: `blank_session()` for an isolated blank schema, or `SessionLocal` inside a rolled-back transaction. Seed REAL FK targets - Postgres enforces constraints sqlite would have silently ignored. Mock-chain tests (`qm.filter.return_value = qm`) break silently when a query gains `.order_by()`.
- **CI's database has NO data (PRINCIPLES.md governs the rule).** The local `DATABASE_URL` is a prod copy, so a borrowed `LIMIT 1` lookup resolves to something real locally and `None` on CI - one borrowed lookup produced 16 failures once. Every test seeds its own chain with a marker prefix; if the suite needs genuinely shared reference data, run the seeding migration's `upgrade()` in a rolled-back transaction rather than assuming a live row.
- **A migration-seeded reference table needs `__company_shared__ = True`, or its own seeds are invisible to a scoped user.** `build_company_predicate` (`app/services/company_scope.py`) compiles an owned table to `company_id IN (scope)`, excluding NULL-company migration rows; only `__company_shared__` adds `OR company_id IS NULL`. Symptom reads as an auth bug (API-key caller sees the seeds, logged-in user sees none) rather than a scoping one.
- **Suffixed NextAuth session cookie breaks `getToken` -> refresh-logout.** `NEXTAUTH_COOKIE_SUFFIX` renames the cookie so :3000/:3001 don't clobber each other, but any `getToken()` caller using the default name finds nothing -> 401 after a hard refresh while `/api/auth/session` still looks fine. Single source of truth: `lib/auth-cookie.ts` `sessionTokenCookieName()`, passed as `cookieName` everywhere - never hardcode `next-auth.session-token`.
- **Deep-link-after-login is the `(protected)` layout's job**, redirecting to `/signin?callbackUrl=<pathname+search+hash>` - capture the full relative URL or query strings get dropped. Portal contact links (`/view`, `/portal`) live under `(auth)`, a separate NextAuth-independent flow.
- **Every Respond.io send must write an `integration_log` on success AND failure**, even a 401 from bad local creds - mirror `_send_and_log`. The raised exception is stamped with the actually-attempted payload so the outbox shows the truth. `integration_log.business_id` is a UUID column - use `notification.id`, never a composite string.
- **Respond sends use the WORKSPACE key, not env `RESPOND_API_KEY`.** `RespondClient.for_identifier(...)` resolves the per-contact/default workspace key first; the env key is a deprecated last-resort fallback. A bad workspace key 401s every send while `settings.respond_api_key` stays valid.
- **Form-SLA stage is identified by `(source_entity_type, team_set_code)`**, not tier alone - `AccessAgentService.resolve_team_with_tier_fallback(agent, start_tier, team_set)` walks up from the tracker's tier to the first team that exists, used by both initial assignment and escalation so a missing intermediate tier is skipped, not fatal.
- **SLA notify is a matrix: stage bool AND per-user event toggle.** Stage `notify_assignee`/`notify_on_escalation` gate the event; per-user `notify_email_on_{assignment,escalation}`/`notify_whatsapp_on_{...}` gate the channel. In-app always sends when the stage allows; WhatsApp additionally needs a linked RespondContact.
- **Staff team-notification emails link to the in-system detail page, never the public `/view?token=` page** - recipients are internal staff and the deep-link-after-login carries them back post-login. Each entity keeps `_build_*_internal_url` separate from `_build_*_view_url`.
- **Status pill colour is centralized in `lib/status-pill.ts`** (soft pastel), reused across PR/SF/stock-inquiry list + detail. `getDisplayStatus` must prioritize the terminal lifecycle `status` over `approval_status` or list/detail/portal disagree.
- **react-query staleness on entity mutation: key dependent queries on the entity's changing field** (e.g. `updated_at`/`status`), not just the entity id - otherwise a banner reflecting a spawned SLA stage shows the OLD stage's reason until a manual refresh.
- **MCP `updated_at` must be emitted as naive Malaysia wall-clock, not offset-aware `+08:00`.** An aware `...+08:00` gets re-converted back to UTC by downstream n8n/luxon consumers, undoing the conversion. Fixed generically at the `updated_at` key in `_sanitize_tool_response`, not per-tool.
- **Complaint <-> DO auto-fulfilment invariants.** (1) "Delivered" needs BOTH `actual_delivery_date` set AND `order_status` in {delivered, completed}. (2) The auto-linker only touches `LINKABLE_STATUSES = {processed_by_cs, fulfilled}` - a `submitted` complaint won't retro-link without a re-save of the DO. (3) The team delivery email sends ONE email per member as To - CC recipients were silently dropped. (4) Notify tiers: DB -> env -> default `1,2`.
- **MCP stock-balance hides on-hand=0 rows zeroed by a `SYSTEM_ADJUSTMENT`** via `exclude_zero_system_adjustment=true` (default true for MCP, false for the FE list) - a genuine 0 from a real sale/import is still returned.
- **AI assistant prompts live in a DB registry (`app/services/ai_prompt_registry.py`), not hardcoded.** Immutable versions + movable `production`/`staging` labels; `get_prompt(db,name,label)` TTL-caches with a hardcoded fallback when DB-unreachable. `config.system_prompt` is deprecated/read-ignored - the `agent_system` registry key is the source of truth.
- **The prompt dry-run (`.../prompts/{name}/test`) runs the WHOLE assistant turn end-to-end**, not a single node - you see only the final synthesizer answer, using the SAVED selected version (not the unsaved editor buffer), and it strips write-capable MCP tools (`*_submit`/`*_create`/`*_link`) so a test can't persist a real record.
- **Prompt-registry save-validation returns a TOP-LEVEL body, not the `AppException` envelope** - `POST .../prompts/{name}/versions` on an unknown `{{token}}` bypasses `response_model` via a raw `JSONResponse` (`422 {error, unknown_tokens, missing_vars}`). FE must read those fields directly, not via `extractApiError`.
- **Form handling-lock "escalated" = `escalated_at` stamped, NOT `current_tier > 1`.** Some form-SLA configs START above tier 1 (project_sales begins at tier 2; PR/SF routes to a default approver at their own tier) - a fresh, never-escalated tracker can legitimately sit at tier 2/3. Gate on `escalated_at` everywhere (FE `resolveHandlingLockState`, BE `handling_lock_service._is_escalated()`), set only by `_escalate_tracker`.
- **The in-form lock banner and the SLA-escalation banner are TWO separate queries** - a manual "Escalate" must invalidate both (`useHandlingLock().refresh()` alongside the SLA query) or the lock banner lags a reload even though the SLA banner updates live.
- **An `async def` route that never awaits blocks its WHOLE worker's event loop** - symptom is a 504/queuing pattern (measured 61s apart), not one slow response, because prod runs 4 gunicorn workers and one blocks for the handler's duration. Fix is plain `def` (anyio threadpools it) or `run_in_threadpool`, capped to the DB pool or 504s just become "too many clients". ~40 handlers remain unconverted (BL-009) and the pattern decays back in - treat new heavy sync work in `async def` as a defect on sight.
- **On macOS an RQ work-horse SEGFAULTS the moment it opens a NEW psycopg2 connection**, if the parent already touched XPC/GSS (`ENABLE_SCHEDULER=true` guarantees this). RQ reports only `waitpid returned 11`; the job never marks failed and its row stays `processing` forever. Fix: `PGGSSENCMODE=disable`. A second, distinct fork-unsafe path (`getproxies()` via boto3/requests) needs `no_proxy='*'`. Linux is unaffected.
- **A docstring asserting a performance number is load-bearing and goes stale silently.** A flyer-read docstring claimed "~1s, stops holding at ~10s"; measured reality was 17-18s and nothing caught the drift because nothing failed. Record what a number was measured against, and re-measure before reusing it in a new design decision.
- **One container, several suppliers: `inbound_shipment_lines.supplier_id` owns the line.** Line key is `(shipment_id, product_id, supplier_id) NULLS NOT DISTINCT` (migration 374); an upload replaces only its own supplier's lines. Header `supplier_id` is DERIVED (mixed suppliers -> NULL) - never filter shipments by the header alone, use `shipment_supplier_predicate`.
- **A reusable `exists()` predicate needs an explicit `.correlate(<parent>)`** when shared across queries of different shapes - `shipment_supplier_predicate` auto-correlated fine standalone but raised "no FROM clauses due to auto-correlation" once nested inside a query whose outer FROM was already a subquery.
- **A baseline `git checkout <commit>` in a shared worktree leaves it detached, and later commits silently land off the branch.** Compare with `git stash`/`git show <rev>:<path>`/a throwaway `git worktree add` instead of checking out a bare commit in a tree others are committing to.
- **Alembic head revision id over 32 chars is a CI failure, not a style opinion** - `alembic_version.version_num` is `varchar(32)`; `tests/test_alembic_revision_ids.py` gates only the HEAD. Keep new ids short even when the filename stays long (`393_po_schedule_extractor_page_text.py` declares `revision = "393_extractor_page_text"`).
- **A dropdown over a large catalog must never be a capped static list - use a server-searched `SearchableSelect`.** `GET /master-data/products/select` defaults `DEFAULT_LIMIT = 100` against ~22,000 products; a picker that loads once and filters client-side answers "no results" for 99.5% of the catalog and looks like a search bug, not a paging one (hit twice: attachment linking, and a promotion picker fed `pageSize:1000`). Use async `SearchableSelect` with server `fetchOptions`, `paginated`, and a `selectedOption` fallback. Reference: `services/scmOptionsService.ts::searchProductOptions`.
- **A raw `text()` INSERT in a test skips every Python-side model default, and only CI notices.** `suppliers.is_active` (`default=True`, no server default) is filled by the ORM but not a raw insert; the dev DB (a prod copy) forgives it, CI's `create_all` schema rejects it. Seed through the model.
- **A pattern kill from one lane kills every lane** - `pkill -f next-server`/`uvicorn`/`worker.py` has no idea which worktree it is standing in and takes down every dev server on the machine with no error to the victim, just a dead port. **Never kill by pattern.** Kill by port (`lsof -ti :PORT | xargs kill`) or an explicit PID you started, and leave a port-probe watchdog running if a lane's server keeps dying under you.

## Extracted 2026-07-13, cross-repo and general gotchas

These were split out of `CLAUDE.md` in the first extraction. As binding as the rest.

- **Pydantic drops an unknown field name silently - a payload key typo becomes a missing value, not an error.** When two services exchange JSON the field names must match byte-for-byte; grep the RECEIVING schema, don't assume. A test asserting the wrong key freezes the bug in place until the assertion itself is corrected.
- **A URL-fragment credential collides with a component that appends a query string.** `/embed/ideas/{id}#token=<TOK>` plus a nav component appending `?ctx=...` folds the query INTO the fragment and corrupts the token. Fix: don't thread the token through in-page navigation URLs - persist it in an in-memory store on first load, read store-first on every route mount, keep nav paths plain.
- **A backgrounded uvicorn without `--reload` runs stale code** - a "fix didn't work" that's really "the fix never loaded". Restart the API (or start with `--reload`) after a backend edit before concluding the change is wrong; restarting the worker but not the API gives the SAME symptom, since each process has its own staleness window (`ps -p <pid> -o lstart=` vs `stat -f %Sm <file>`).
- **An unhandled backend 500 reads as a CORS error in the browser.** `CORSMiddleware` only attaches ACAO headers to responses it wraps; a request that raises past it (e.g. `ResponseValidationError`) produces a bare 500 with no CORS headers, so the browser reports a CORS error and hides the real one. Always read the backend log for the actual traceback before chasing a CORS config.
- **A reusable physical identifier needs the identity triple, not just the identifier** - "reusable once closed" is exactly where duplicates get in. A packing-list PDF re-uploaded after GRN fell through a container-only match (containers ARE reusable once received) and created a duplicate shipment. Fix: a RECEIVED shipment whose `(container, ETA, shipment_date)` triple equals the payload is a duplicate upload -> `409`; any date difference is a genuinely new shipment.
- **n8n writes integration errors into `response_payload`, but every user-facing surface reads the `error_code`/`error_message` COLUMNS.** The n8n error branch never sets those columns, so a real reason sits behind "View raw log" while the UI shows a bare "Integration failed". Fix is two-sided: the backend stamps the columns itself before raising (safe - n8n's follow-up POST can't clobber them via `exclude_unset=True`), and the FE falls back to `response_payload.error` when the column is NULL.
- **A new service-layer exception must be handled at EVERY route that calls the service, or a bare `except Exception` turns it into a 500 for one caller and a clean error for another.** `grep` every caller before shipping a new domain exception, and pin it with a test per caller.
- **Verifying "these failures are pre-existing" requires capturing the failure LIST, not the summary line.** `pytest -q | tail -3` keeps only the count; every later `grep FAILED` against it returns nothing, which reads as "no failures" when it means "no data". Capture `pytest -q | grep '^FAILED' | sort` on both sides and `comm -23` them.
- **The Bash tool's cwd persists across calls, so a `cd sub/dir && ...` silently invalidates later repo-root paths.** A follow-up `git status --porcelain -- path` or `git log -- path` after an unnoted `cd` prints empty output, indistinguishable from "clean/never committed". Anchor path-sensitive git commands with an explicit `cd <repo-root> &&`.
- **A manual probe against a stale dev DB can be unfalsifiable - it returns the miss value whether the code is right or hardcoded to fail.** Before reading a null/empty result as a verdict on the code, count the rows that satisfy every predicate in the query; if there are none, seed one (marker-scoped) so the guard has a case it CAN fail.
- **`git add` and `git commit` in separate tool calls are not atomic when anything else shares the repo** - a concurrent branch checkout between the two resets the index and "nothing added to commit" can mean the edits are still sitting in the working tree, not lost. Combine `add && commit` into one invocation; verify with `git rev-parse HEAD` against `origin/<branch>` rather than trusting push output.
- **An index created by raw `op.execute` in a migration is invisible in the model** - `__table_args__` under-reports what's actually indexed. Query `pg_indexes` or run `EXPLAIN` before concluding an index is missing; a model/DB drift here is a separate finding from whatever you were actually debugging.
- **A field written by an allowlist and read by a manual serializer must be in BOTH lists, and only a whole-set assertion catches the gap.** Naming fields one at a time is how this recurs (portal `pic` then `sales_type` hit the identical gap twice). Assert `set(_editable_fields(kind)) - set(_serialize_request_detail(row))` is empty, which prints the offending name on failure.
- **Every worktree shares one Redis, so an RQ job can be executed by a worker whose branch lacks the task function.** It goes to RQ's FAILED registry silently (`llen` reads 0), while the downstream row sits `pending` forever with no error surfaced. Diagnose with `FailedJobRegistry(queue=q).get_job_ids()` vs your own `worker_name`; `reg.requeue(jid)` fixes it. Real fix is per-worktree queue names.
- **Claude-managed background Bash tasks are reaped when the turn ends - a long-lived dev server must be detached.** Launch with `nohup ... > log 2>&1 < /dev/null & disown`, then verify with `lsof -ti :PORT` and an HTTP probe, not the task status.
- **A per-row query inside a serializer loop is an N+1 no test notices, and a column headed with an entity name must count DISTINCT entities, not join rows.** A promotions list issued one `COUNT` per row (12 rows -> 15 queries) AND separately over-counted "Products" via `count(promotion_products.id)` (a real cross-group extra row, not a duplicate to delete). Batch via `GROUP BY`; pin the query count with a `before_cursor_execute` listener (`<= 1`), never a wall-clock assertion.
- **A long unbroken token breaks layout two different ways, and both need the item to shrink FIRST.** In a fixed-layout table, `overflow-wrap: anywhere` (not `break-word`) is what lowers a cell's min-content width so `auto` sizing stays safe. In a CSS grid, an item defaults to `min-width: auto`, so `break-words` alone does nothing until the item also gets `min-w-0`. Verify by measurement (`scrollWidth` vs `clientWidth`/`getBoundingClientRect`), not by eye.
- **A consumer written against a shape the producer never emits fails silently and forever - the absent key just reads as the default.** An MCP presenter read a nested `certificate{}` key the backend never sent, so an expired-in-2016 certificate reported `"expired": false` with no error (the presenter's own tests used hand-written rows that DID contain the key). Two-sided shapes need a test on the PRODUCING side, not just the consumer.
- **An MCP list filter must be registered in TWO places, and forgetting the second one is an empty page, not an error.** A query param needs both the ToolSpec's `query_params` AND `TOOL_REQUIRED_NARROWING_FILTERS` in `server.py` - without the second, a call scoped only by that filter returns `{"data": []}` while the backend filter works fine, and the agent answers a silent wrong "no results" rather than erroring.
- **A list that opens with a default (opinionated) filter cannot be reconciled against another source, and the mismatch reads as data loss.** If a list's row count is something a human will compare externally (files on disk, a manifest), it must open UNFILTERED with the opinionated view as a filter-dropdown option, not the default.
- **Pushing to a branch after its PR has merged orphans the commit with no warning from any tool.** `gh pr view <n> --json state,mergedAt` before pushing follow-on work to an existing PR branch; if merged, cut a fresh branch from `origin/main` and cherry-pick, and verify with `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/main` rather than trusting the push output.
- **A fixed `grid-cols-N` tab list collapses variable-length labels instead of overflowing visibly**, so it looks fine in every desktop screenshot until one more tab tips it over. Wrap by breakpoint (`grid-cols-2 sm:grid-cols-3 lg:grid-cols-5` + `h-auto`) and measure the tablist's `scrollWidth` vs `clientWidth` at 375px rather than eyeballing it.

## Retired

Kept for the record. Do NOT follow these - each is superseded by an entry above or a rule now
governed by `PRINCIPLES.md`/`CLAUDE.md`.

- **Playwright MCP can disconnect mid-session** - superseded by agent-browser verification (`CLAUDE.md` "Browser verification"); Playwright MCP is retired for verification, so its disconnect behaviour no longer applies.
- **sqlite pytest fixtures** - superseded by "Tests run on Postgres ONLY, NEVER sqlite" (`PRINCIPLES.md`); the sqlite-fixture workaround this described is now a banned approach, not a recipe.

## 89. A bootstrap assertion that names a rule dies the day the rule is retired (27 Aug 2026)

`scripts/bootstrap_env.py._fix_committed_v` asserted a hard-coded marker string as proof the newest `scm.committed_v` body had landed; migration 424 retired that leg on purpose, so every branch carrying 424 aborted CI in bootstrap before a single test ran, reading as test failures. Now asserts the current marker, but it is still a hard-coded substring - the same trap fires again next time the view is redefined. Prefer asserting on something the source-of-truth module exports.

## 90. CI's database is `bootstrap_env`, not the migrations - a view a migration redefines stays old on CI until bootstrap mirrors it (28 Aug 2026)

`scripts/bootstrap_env.py.create_views()` replays view DDL BY HAND and can lag a migration that used `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` - migration 420 redefined `scm.on_order_v` (LEFT JOIN) while bootstrap still built 337's body (INNER JOIN), so a drill-total test passed on the dev copy and failed only on CI. No CI check enforces the mirror. When a migration touches a view, update `bootstrap_env.create_views()` in the SAME commit, and reproduce a CI-only red from a from-zero database rather than trusting the dev copy.

## 91. The local Postgres runs `TimeZone = Asia/Seoul`, so a `now()` probe against a naive UTC timestamp lies by nine hours (28 Aug 2026)

`now()` is `timestamptz` converted through the session zone; a column that is `timestamp without time zone` holding UTC compared with `now()` shifts by the session's offset - locally hidden (Seoul), exposed on CI (UTC). Probe naive-UTC columns with `clock_timestamp() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC'`, never `now()`.

## 92. Under `from __future__ import annotations`, a pydantic field named after its own type resolves to itself (30 Aug 2026)

A field literally called `date` in a module with `from __future__ import annotations` makes every annotation a STRING resolved later against the module namespace - by then `date` is the field, not `datetime.date`, so `date: Optional[date]` reads as "must be None" and every dated value fails `response_model` validation while the service computed the right answer all along. Import compiles fine, which makes the tell misleading. Alias the type on the way in (`from datetime import date as DateType`) - the same trap waits on any field named `id`, `type` or `list` in a `__future__`-annotated schema module.

## 93. The venv is Python 3.14; CI is 3.12 - an f-string that reuses its own quote inside `{}` collects locally and is a SyntaxError on CI (30 Aug 2026)

`f"... {d["k"]}"` passes on 3.14 (nested same-quote expressions are allowed) and breaks `Validate backend imports` on 3.12 with `SyntaxError: f-string: unmatched '['`, taking an unrelated file down through the import while tests stay green. Use the other quote inside the braces (`{d['k']}`); compile changed files with a real 3.12 before pushing - a regex audit is not a parser.

## 94. A motion pass that samples mid-animation proves nothing about the end states (31 Aug 2026)

A sidebar collapse passed browser review because the tester sampled mid-collapse frames; both real defects lived in the AFTER states. Verify interactions as ROUND-TRIPS and measure final geometry (`getBoundingClientRect`, computed transform) in every end state - mid-animation screenshots are supporting evidence only, and a fix touching a mechanism re-verifies the mechanism's whole interaction, not just the symptom that was reported.

## 95. A per-migration test that asserts "X is the single head" fails on the very next migration (2 Sep 2026)

`test_453_is_the_single_head_of_the_whole_graph` asserted `heads == ['453_...']`; true the day it was written, false the moment a later migration chained onto 453. The property wanted is "the graph has one head and my migration is an ANCESTOR of it" - assert `len(heads) == 1` and walk `down_revision` from the head, never assert equality with a specific head id. The single-head fast gate in CI already covers the "one head" half.

## 96. A rule that only fires when a sibling rung FAILS gives two answers to one question (3 Sep 2026)

The SCM reorder ladder asked the asking bin's own site pool at step 0 but left OTHER site pools to a later spill step, reached only if earlier rungs had all failed - so the SAME rule answered two lines of one order two different ways depending on whether a sibling rung happened to succeed. State a rung's SCOPE up front and walk all of it there; a rung placed behind "if nothing else worked" is conditioned on facts unrelated to it, the tell that it is two rules wearing one name. The repair moved the whole chain into step 0 and deleted the spill, rather than adding a second trigger.

## 97. Migration tests running real DDL deadlock under xdist against OTHER files' SELECTs, and `--dist loadfile` only serializes within one file (5 Sep 2026)

Several `tests/test_migration_*.py` files run real `ALTER TABLE` / `DROP COLUMN` through `pg_session` against shared tables, holding the AccessExclusiveLock until the test's transaction rolls back. Run 33894859525 (main) died with `psycopg2.errors.DeadlockDetected`: the 400 test's `ALTER TABLE projects.order_inquiry_rows DROP COLUMN` on one xdist worker collided with `tests/test_order_inquiry_place_on_po.py`'s SELECT on another worker, and Postgres killed the DDL side. `--dist loadfile` serializes the tests OF one file; it does nothing for two different files landing on two different workers. Fix: `tests/test_migration_*.py` is excluded from the xdist step (`--ignore-glob`) and run in its own serial step afterward, on shard 2 only, since the whole set is a few seconds of test time. Adding a new `test_migration_*.py` file needs no registration - the glob covers it.

## 98. Calling a FastAPI route function in process skips its router dependencies, so the caller must set what they would have set (6 Sep 2026)

The chatbot turn engine calls the resolver ROUTE (`resolve_reference_post`) directly on its own session, deliberately, so the spec-search fallback and the entity-pin check are not re-implemented. What came with it: `apply_company_scope`, `get_current_user` and the module guard are ROUTER dependencies and none of them runs on an in-process call. The session therefore read `UNSET`, `build_company_predicate` compiles that to `false()` for every `CompanyScopedMixin` model, and every business turn answered "Couldn't find: `<code>` (product)" for products that exist in the contact's own company - in prod and locally, invisible to a large chatbot test corpus because the tests stubbed that seam. An in-process route call must set what its dependencies would have set, from the SAME function the dependency uses (here `company_scope_resolver.resolve_contact_company_scope`, one mechanism, two callers), and the test must assert it against a NON-default company: `tests/conftest.py` defaults every new session's scope to Sorento, so "the scope is not UNSET" passes on a fix that never ran.

## 99. CI vitest gate retries a failed test twice; three failures in a row is real (6 Sep 2026)

Five of six deploy runs on 2026-09-06 (34008077286, 34008475205, 34009224785, 34010205328, 34015767197) were each blocked by ONE different test - RequestTagDesigner Fix B (x2), SubmissionForm plural count (x2), TagTemplatesList bulk-delete Cancel - all timing out the same 5s async wait, and all pass 15/15 in a local loop. The runner is 2-vCPU under a ~10.5k-test suite, not a logic bug. Fix is `retry: process.env.CI ? 2 : 0` in `vitest.config.ts`: local stays 0 so a flake is visible while it is being written, CI retries a failed test up to twice before it counts. Read the gate accordingly: a "flaky" mark in the CI summary means the test passed on retry and deserves a look, not a block; a red gate means the test failed three times in a row and is a real failure.

## 100. A shared retrieval pool is not the place to enforce ONE consumer's safety rule (6 Sep 2026)

The chatbot picks one MCP tool per turn as the argmax of cosine similarity over `embedding_chunks` and calls the top hit, and the pool held six write tools (`crm_order_cancel`, `crm_complaint_close`, the two purchase-request approvals, an IT ticket create, an ideation turn) - so a customer sentence that happened to score one would have cancelled an order. The obvious fix, filtering them out at pool-build time, was wrong twice over: the in-app AI assistant retrieves from that SAME pool and a bootstrap puts those tools in it on purpose (it confirms each with a human first), and a pool filter is DATA, so it changes nothing in production until somebody re-seeds. Enforce a consumer's rule on THAT consumer's retrieval and call seams, and leave the shared substrate alone. Two more traps in the same fix: derive "is this safe to call" from a DECLARATION, not the HTTP method (three of these POSTs take a body only because it will not fit in a query string), and do not read the source-of-truth file at request time if it is not in the deployed image - `sorento_crm_mcp` is not in the backend container, so a catalogue walk on the turn path would have failed every live turn. Freeze the list in the consumer and let a CI test assert it equals the source of truth, where that source is actually readable.

## 101. A dry run must preview the DECISION, not only the values - the console is where the owner tests (6 Sep 2026)

The escalation lane evaluated its dry-run branch first (H37's own ordering: never reach a writing seam) and built the preview actions from the team the ladder had already carried in. Everything after that branch - including the new gate that stops an escalation inheriting the previous turn's team - was live-only. The owner tests from the console, and the console runs `is_test`, so the very defect the gate exists to fix was the one thing they would still have seen: "escalate to Nurain" previewed an assignment to `purchasing`, exactly as before, while pytest was green on all four arms of the gate. The rule that survives is narrower than "run everything on a dry run": a dry run must take every READ-only decision the live turn takes, and suppress only the WRITES. Reads (a staff lookup, a round-robin cursor read) are what make a preview worth showing; skipping a decision because it sits after the guard turns the preview into a different turn from the one being previewed. The second half of the same lesson: the check that caught it was a real turn through a real backend, and it caught it because a lane backend booted without `--reload` served the OLD code for one run - restart it, or the evidence is of the previous commit.

## 102. A port's tests must cross the PRODUCTION seam with the PRODUCTION shape (6 Sep 2026)

Three fixes shipped green in #700 and were bypassed on the first live turn, because every test that proved them stubbed the seam with the shape the n8n NODE emits, not the shape the CRM SERVICE returns. `MCPRuntimeClient.call_tool` returns a STRING (`"\n".join(content[].text)`), and the four probe seams handed it straight to `run_crossdomain`, whose `isinstance(probe_result, dict)` guard dropped it - so every cross-domain answer rendered as `no_envelope`, and the stub that returned `{"answers": [], "has_result": False}` said nothing about it. `ProductService.list_products` returns `{"data": [Product ORM objects]}`, and `jsc.get(row, "product_code")` returns its default on anything that is not a dict, so the sibling-family offer was never built - the stub returned dicts. And the probe sent `sub-get-results`' workflowInputs as the MCP tool arguments: measured against the live MCP, the server answers those with `{"data": [], "total": 0}` and only `entity_ids_transformer`'s arguments earn the render envelope. A test that hand-builds the upstream node's JSON proves the port reads n8n; it proves nothing about the CRM. Cross the real seam - the real service on the pg fixture, or a fake returning a real captured payload - and where the seam is a sub-workflow boundary, run the sub's first node at the seam rather than at the four ported call sites whose captures grade their own output.

## 103. A migration seeding a reference row can change chatbot resolution - a console check must follow EVERY deploy, not only chatbot PRs (7 Sep 2026)

#713 (chatbot console pass 4) deployed clean and the chatbot console check was run against it. The SAME deploy also carried #707's migration `485_shipment_line_photo_type.py`, an unrelated SCM feature seeding a new `attachment_types` row ("Shipment Line Photo") that happened to share the substring "photo" with the pre-existing "Product Photos" row - and three minutes after the deploy, "send me the photo of SRTWC8517-SH-UF" stopped resolving deterministically (a silent wrong pick, or a did-you-mean for a document type the customer never asked about) where the SAME request had worked cleanly just before. `git diff` on #713's own files showed nothing wrong, because nothing in #713 was wrong - the regression was #707's, entirely, and #707 had no chatbot involvement to prompt a chatbot check against it. The chatbot's entity resolver (`entity_resolver.py`) is SHARED with every other admin-data reference table, so any migration that seeds or edits `attachment_types`, or any other table the resolver's Tier 1/2 probes search, is chatbot-relevant whether or not its own PR touches a chatbot file. `documentation/agents/chatbot-verification.md`'s console check now runs after EVERY deploy, not only a chatbot PR's own.

## 104. A reviewer's kill-test mutation in a shared worktree gets committed by someone else (7 Sep 2026)

On the SPO supersede lane the reviewer ran a kill test the way the agent file said to: edit `procurement_service.py` in place (the D28b approval gate replaced by a bare filter marked `# KILLTEST`), run the test, `git checkout --` the file. The coder and the captain were live in the same worktree. The captain's scripted edit to a DIFFERENT block of the same file read the mutated text, wrote it back with the fix on top, ran the lane tests green (with the gate missing), and then `git add`ed the file; the reviewer's restore landed in between the edit and the add, so the commit carried the mutation and not the fix. Two facts made it invisible: the test list stayed green because AC-X28 seeded an APPROVED header and never exercised the draft case the gate existed for, and `git status` was clean afterwards because the restore had run. The reviewer found it by reading its own diff. Rules now in `.claude/agents/reviewer.md`: a kill test never touches a file another agent can commit; mutate a scratch copy or a throwaway worktree. And for the captain: `git add <path>` on a file another agent is known to be editing is a merge, not a commit; read `git diff <path>` before adding it.

## 105. A shared service method that commits must never be called inside a savepoint (12 Sep 2026)

`planning_change_service.apply()` wraps each order in `db.begin_nested()`; the per-order helper called `_notify_purchasing` before `savepoint.commit()`, and `NotificationService.create_with_channel_preferences` ends with an unconditional `self.db.commit()`. That inner commit closed the savepoint's own transaction, so the caller's `savepoint.commit()` raised `ResourceClosedError` ("This transaction is closed"), and the per-order try/except reported a cleanly applied order as failed. It only surfaced with a real `purchasing`-role user seeded - every other planning-change test never had one, so the path went unexercised. Fix: notify AFTER the savepoint has committed, not inside it, still best-effort so a notify failure cannot undo an applied order.

## 106. A 'use client' component file must export components only (13 Sep 2026)

Exporting a plain helper (`productFallbackFor`) from `SalesOrderDetail.tsx` (2420ee00f) made Next log "[Fast Refresh] performing full reload" and every edit or fast-forward under the dev server wiped the open edit session (`isEditing`, drafts, `removedLineIds`), so Save looked dead with a clean console. jsdom cannot show it - the failure only exists under the real dev server's Fast Refresh boundary. Fix (6c6f5643d): move the helper to `salesOrderLineDraft.ts`, a plain module, and leave the component file exporting components only. Check the dev-server console for "performing full reload" when a button "does nothing" with no console error; and never edit the served worktree while someone is mid-edit in the browser - a full reload during that session is the same wipe even when the edit itself is correct.

## 107. A service-level link cache needs invalidating on EVERY path that deletes or shrinks a link, not only the obvious one (13 Sep 2026)

`ProjectOrderInquiryService._invalidate_link_cache` exists so a total already changed in this pass cannot be read stale by the next write in the same pass - every writer of a link is supposed to call it. `_remove_links` did; `_unclaim_shares` (`planning_change_service.py`, the rule-6 re-deal seam) deleted or shrank links and called `refresh_link_state`, but never `_invalidate_link_cache`. One `_redeal_document` pass that split a freed document across a waiting row and then the pool called `place_on_po_allocations` twice - the second call read `_candidates_for_row`'s memo from BEFORE the first delete, saw the purchase-order line as still fully claimed, and refused with `order_inquiry_po_line_short`, failing the whole order. The tell: a `failed_orders` entry naming a line whose links, read straight from the DB afterwards, already look free - the code failed on a memo, not on the data. Fix: invalidate the cache right beside the existing flush and `refresh_link_state`, in the same place the delete happens. Guard any link-deleting path with a test that forces a SECOND placement in the same pass (a two-leg redeal, not a single one), or the staleness never gets exercised.

## 108. Never keyboard-type into a native date input under agent-browser (13 Sep 2026)

Typing into a native `<input type="date">` crashed the session's own headless Chromium twice in one walk. Set the value through the native setter (`Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(HTMLInputElement.prototype, 'value').set.call(el, 'YYYY-MM-DD')`) then dispatch `input` and `change`, never `fill` or a keystroke sequence. If a session's Chromium dies anyway, kill only that session's own Chrome PID pair (its `agent-browser-chrome-<uuid>` user-data-dir), never the shared daemon, then reopen under the same session name and log in again.

## 109. Measure inside a Dialog with a callback ref, not useEffect + useRef (14 Sep 2026)

The shared `DialogContent` mirrors Radix's open state into React state to gate its exit spring, so the content mounts one commit AFTER `open` flips. An effect keyed on `open` reads a null ref, the ResizeObserver never attaches, and the surface opens at the wrong size (the r9 design lightbox opened at 100% wearing a "Fit" label and overflowed at 375px). Attach observers through a callback ref that fires when the node actually exists.

## 110. Switch a lane's pytest database with `${VAR:-default}` in the worktree .env (14 Sep 2026)

`app/main.py` loads `.env` with `override=True`, so an exported `DATABASE_URL` is silently discarded and pytest runs against whatever the .env names, which on a lane is the shared prod copy. python-dotenv expands POSIX defaults, so write `DATABASE_URL=${PTAG9_DB_URL:-postgresql://...shared...}` (and the same for `DIRECT_URL`) in the lane .env: `PTAG9_DB_URL=... venv/bin/pytest` hits the private DB while the running uvicorn (no var) keeps the shared one. Verified: `import app.main; settings.database_url` answers each DB by the presence of the var alone.

## 111. A service that reads a relationship it just wrote must attach to the relationship, not rely on a flush (16 Sep 2026)

`SessionLocal` is `autoflush=False` (`app/database.py`). `_add_line_parts` did `db.add(PriceTagRequestLinePart(line_id=line.id, ...))` and the very next call read `line.parts` to find open choice groups; the lazy load SELECTed before the pending rows existed, returned `[]`, and every request submitted through the portal got one tag with empty choices. Every route test passed because `blank_session()` is `autoflush=True`. Two browser passes, a tester bisect of the payload and a Sonnet diagnosis all looked at the payload; the payload was never the variable. Fix: `line.parts.append(...)` so the in-memory object is authoritative in the unit of work. Rule: when a service populates rows and reads them back in the same transaction, attach through the relationship; and the regression test for such a path runs under the app's own flush policy (`session.autoflush = False`), or it proves nothing.

## 112. vitest: a Radix surface left open at the end of a test file crashes the job after the last test passes (17 Sep 2026)

Every test in `FulfilmentBoardPanel.undo.test.tsx` ended with a Radix DropdownMenu still open. Testing Library's auto cleanup unmounts it after the last test, which arms FocusScope's own unmount effect: `setTimeout(() => container.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent(...)), 0)`. On a loaded CI runner vitest can tear the jsdom environment down before that 0ms timer fires, so the CustomEvent gets built against an already-dead realm and jsdom's `dispatchEvent` throws "parameter 1 is not of type 'Event'" as an unhandled error, failing a job whose 3214 tests all passed. It never reproduced locally because an idle machine wins the race every time. Fix: `vitest.setup.ts` now runs `cleanup()` then drains one real macrotask (`await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 0))`) in a global `afterEach`, so the timer fires while the window is still alive. Rule: leaving a Dialog/DropdownMenu/Popover/Sheet open at a test file's end is fine, the setup drain covers it; a test that asserts on the unmount timer itself must use fake timers, which the drain skips (`vi.isFakeTimers()`).

## 113. SQLAlchemy JSON/JSONB stores Python None as the JSON literal null unless none_as_null=True; an isnot(None) guard does not see it, and jsonb_array_length throws (17 Sep 2026)

`SOSupplyDecision.undo_journal` (`Column(JSONB, nullable=True)`) was cleared with Core SQL `.values(undo_journal=None)` at two sites in `project_supply_undo_service.py` (`UndoJournal.attach`, `undo_last_confirm`). SQLAlchemy's JSON type default (`none_as_null=False`) serialises a Python `None` VALUE as the JSON literal `null`, not a SQL NULL - the column itself was never NULL, it held a JSON scalar. `_journalled_decision_clause`'s guard, `undo_journal.isnot(None)`, read true for that row (it is not SQL NULL), so the next clause, `jsonb_array_length(undo_journal) > 0`, ran on a JSON `null` and Postgres raised `InvalidParameterValue: cannot get array length of a scalar` - 500ing the fulfilment planning board read for any order carrying one (shipped to prod in #985 04:37Z). It survived review because reading the column back through the ORM masks it completely: SQLAlchemy's JSON type deserialises a stored JSON `null` back to Python `None` on the way out, so `decision.undo_journal is None` reads true either way - only a raw SQL read (`... IS NULL`, `jsonb_typeof(...)`) or Postgres's own `jsonb_array_length` can tell a JSON `null` apart from a real SQL NULL. Fixed (this lane) by declaring the column `JSONB(none_as_null=True)` so a Python `None` write always produces a SQL NULL from here on, a one-time data repair migration (`undo_0003_journal_sql_null`) turning existing JSON-null rows back into SQL NULL, and replacing the guard with a `CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(...) = 'array' THEN jsonb_array_length(...) ELSE 0 END > 0` - a bare `and_(jsonb_typeof(...) == 'array', jsonb_array_length(...) > 0)` does NOT fix this, because Postgres does not guarantee left-to-right evaluation of an `AND`'s branches and can still evaluate the array-length call on a JSON-null row; `CASE` is the one construct SQL guarantees evaluates its branches in order. Rule: any JSONB/JSON column ever cleared with a Python `None` by any path - ORM constructor, ORM attribute assignment, or Core `.values(col=None)` - needs `none_as_null=True` on the column, and any guard mixing `jsonb_typeof`/`jsonb_array_length` in the same `AND` needs a `CASE`, not a bare boolean pair.

## 114. A test that replays migration DDL against the REAL `scm` schema deadlocks another xdist worker's plan read, and `run_reorder` turns that into an empty plan four files away (18 Sep 2026)

Four tests in `tests/scm/test_committed_v_migration_chain.py` replayed six view migrations (340, 346, 384, 423, 424, 426) inside `blank_session()`, which pins `search_path` to its scratch schemas - but a migration names `scm.committed_v` in full, so `search_path` cannot redirect it and `DROP VIEW IF EXISTS scm.committed_v CASCADE` landed on the SHARED database's own view, taking `scm.net_position_v` with it and holding an AccessExclusiveLock on both for the length of the test. `reorder_run_service._planning_rows` reads exactly those two (`keys` is `net_position_v UNION po_ordered_v`, and expanding `net_position_v` reaches `committed_v`), and the two take the pair in opposite orders, so under `-n auto --dist loadfile` Postgres killed one: CI run 35293438670 logged "Process 447: DROP VIEW IF EXISTS scm.committed_v CASCADE" deadlocked against the plan query. Because `run_reorder` RECORDS a failure on the run instead of raising (correct for the RQ worker), the victim - `tests/scm/test_reorder_committed_universe.py` - just read an empty plan and failed on "a named product with zero committed demand must still be planned", with nothing on screen naming the real cause; it passed alone every time, and blocking alone does NOT reproduce it (holding the DROP open for 90s makes the file 270s instead of 40s and all 15 still pass - the lock CYCLE is the failure, not the wait). Fix: the replays run on the session's own scratch `_scm` schema via an `alembic.op` proxy that rewrites each `op.execute` body, so the migration function is still what runs and only where its DDL lands moves; the proxy also ASSERTS that no `scm.` / `projects.` prefix survived the rewrite, because it only knows the two those six bodies use and 376's `_NET_POSITION_V` (`scm.net_position_v`, `scm.on_order_v`) is one statement away from being replayed there too. Rule: a rolled-back transaction is NOT isolation when the statement is DDL - it still holds an AccessExclusiveLock every other worker's reads must queue behind - so any schema-qualified name inside a replayed migration has to be rebound onto the scratch schema, and a swallow-and-record error path (`run_reorder`, any best-effort worker entry point) means the test that fails is not the test that is wrong; read the job's Postgres server log before the assertion message.

## 115. An unbounded `>=` pin on a core library lets a new major release break `main` with no code change (24 Sep 2026)

`sorento_crm_backend/requirements.txt` pinned `sqlalchemy>=2.0.31` with no upper bound. SQLAlchemy 2.1.0 published to PyPI at 20:36Z on 24 Sep 2026, and its `postgresql://` URL now defaults to the `psycopg` (v3) driver instead of `psycopg2`; the repo only installs `psycopg2-binary`, so every backend CI job failed at "Bootstrap the database" with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'psycopg'` from the very next scheduled run (36071672676) - the last green run (16:25Z, same commit range) had resolved 2.0.54. Nothing in the merged PR touched dependencies; the break came purely from an upstream release landing between two runs. Fix: `sqlalchemy>=2.0.31,<2.1` - alembic, the migrations, and every test fixture are written against 2.0 and a driver switch to psycopg v3 is a separate, deliberate decision, not a transitive one. Rule: a core library (ORM, web framework, DB driver) gets an upper bound at the next major version; `fastapi==0.128.0`/`starlette==0.50.0` above already do this for the same reason (see the requirements.txt header comment) - extend the same discipline to every core pin, not just the ones that already bit once.

## 116. Webpack `next dev` (no `--turbopack`) fails pdfjs-dist with "Object.defineProperty called on non-object"; the production build is fine (26 Sep 2026)

Every PDF landed on `PdfViewer`'s error state under a webpack `next dev` server (the mode cloud lanes use, since Turbopack fails on symlinked node_modules). pdf.js threw `TypeError: Object.defineProperty called on non-object` from `__webpack_require__.r` inside `pdfjs-dist/build/pdf.mjs` while the document was loading, and the catch block swallowed it with no trace (PR #1256 review, should-fix finding 4 - now logged via `console.warn`). A `next build` + `next start` on the same code renders every PDF correctly, and CI's `next build` also passes, so this is dev-only under webpack specifically. Rule: if a PDF preview breaks only under `npm run dev` and not `next build`, suspect webpack's dev module wrapper rather than the PDF or the fix itself, and confirm with a prod build before spending time on the pdf.js side.

## 117. A query with no ORDER BY returns Postgres heap order, and heap order moves under xdist or after any UPDATE; a greedy writer fed that list writes different rows on the same input (26 Sep 2026)

`spo_conversion_service._link_ticked_demand` dealt a project row greedily across a shipment line's allocations in the order the list arrived. `revise` built that list from `_own_state`, an `SPOAllocation` query with no ORDER BY, so a Save with nothing changed re-dealt the row's one 40 link as 30 + 10 whenever B came back ahead of A (issue #1289, main runs 36235544908 and 36246124604). Two things put B first: a same-value UPDATE of A (a receive, an earlier revise) did it 20 of 20 times, and under `-n auto` another worker's churn got the page pruned so B reused a freed line pointer ahead of A (`ctid (0,3)` vs `(0,34)`), which is why CI flaked while every isolated run passed. Fix: the dealers order by `_deal_order` (largest first, then warehouse id) and deal rows in key order, so the result depends on the data, not the list order. Rule: anything that allocates, picks "the first", or writes rows off a list must either ORDER BY in its query or be independent of the order it receives. A test that pins the order both ways (monkeypatch the reader to sort ascending and descending) is the deterministic kill test; waiting for the heap to reorder is not.

Second hit, reading side (main deploy cd220251, run 36379111785, 28 Sep 2026): the resolver's exact product probe (`entity_resolver._probe_product`) has no ORDER BY either, and the both-company miss copy names companies in the order its rows come back ("checked in Mocha and Sorento" vs "Sorento and Mocha"; the n8n parity fixtures pin that the answer node keeps the resolver's order, so it is not sorted there). `test_escalation_round6_n8n_behaviour.py` asserted one order in its setup; it passed on its own branch and went red on main only after #1278 added 13 tests with no `.test_durations` entry, which moved pytest-split's shard boundaries and so the history of the worker that ran it. Rule: a test that asserts customer copy built off a resolver list asserts the SET unless the code orders it, and pins both insert orders (seed the rows in each order) when the order matters to the rule under test.

## 118. A queued job that reports `cancelled` with no runner and no steps was never run (GitHub gave up acquiring a hosted runner), it reaches `needs.*.result` as `abandoned`, and a cap sized to the average shard cuts a healthy one (5 Oct 2026)

The first `ci-full` run of CI-MINUTES-CUT (#1492, run 37369427779) taught three things at once. (1) Eleven jobs ended `cancelled` exactly 15:02 after their creation with no runner id and no step run, under caps of 15 AND 35 min, so the cap could not be what fired; the check-run annotation (`gh api repos/<repo>/check-runs/<id>/annotations`) says what did: "The job was not acquired by Runner of type hosted even after multiple attempts". GitHub retries runner assignment for about 15 min and then cancels the job; it happens when the account's 20 concurrent-job slots are held by other runs (three of the five root jobs had waited 11 min for a runner). The first diagnosis blamed the caps ("the clock counts queue time") and pushed 120/90 before reading the annotation. (2) Those jobs, and the matrix whose shard was cut by its cap, reached the `CI gate (full)` job as `needs.<job>.result == "abandoned"`, a value outside the documented success/failure/cancelled/skipped set; the gate's deny-list of failure/cancelled let it pass GREEN on a run GitHub itself marked failure. The gate is now an allow-list (success or skipped, anything else red). (3) Backend shard 2 was cut by the 35-min cap at 94% with progress every 10-40 s, 33:55 of pytest for a shard that took 22 min two days earlier: run-to-run variance is about 1.6x, so a cap at the typical run time is a cap on bad luck. Caps are now about twice the worst observed run (60 on the three backend test jobs, 20 elsewhere). Rules: a `cancelled` job with `runner_id` 0 and no steps is a runner-acquisition failure, never a timeout, read the annotation first; any job that judges `needs.*.result` allow-lists the passing values; and a `timeout-minutes` is sized at twice the worst run, never the average.

## 119. The test and CI schemas are built from the ORM, so a CHECK constraint that lives only in a migration never fires in tests; `audit_logs.action` admits six values and a new one kills the whole write on prod (13 Oct 2026)

PLANNING-WHY (#1600) wrote audit rows with `action = "CANCEL"` and `action = "CONFIRM_REFUSED"`. Prod's `audit_logs_action_check` (`alembic/versions/aud_0001_audit_standard_s0.py:127`) admits only CREATE / READ / UPDATE / DELETE / IMPORT / EVENT, but `scripts/bootstrap_env` and `tests/_pg_fixture.py` build the schema with `create_all`, which has no such CHECK (the model declares none), so 40 green tests and two reviews passed it. The browser pass on the restored prod copy caught it: Simulate confirm on SO422492 died with `CheckViolation`, and because the cancel row is written inside the Confirm's own transaction, every real Confirm that cancels an inquiry row would have failed on prod. Fix: `action = "EVENT"` with the name in the `event` column (precedent `cost_price_change_service.py:1643`), plus a test that reads the allowed set from the migration source. Rules: a new audit write uses one of the six actions and names itself in `event`; before trusting the test schema for a table with migration-only constraints, compare `\d <table>` on a prod copy; and a browser pass on a prod copy is the check that finds this class, not pytest.
